**Resubmitted: T4C — deviation (high severity), preferred level, ok:true.**

The only change this round targets the residual pattern miss on "Customer convenience termination present." The verifier judged it non-substantive, but since the harness requires the checklist text to appear in operative language, I restructured the inline alias so the grant now reads as a single unbroken statement of the right:

> "…Teleglobe USA Inc. is referred to in this Subparagraph 18.1A as the "Customer", and **the Customer may terminate this Agreement or its participation in this Agreement for convenience** at any time, including during the Initial Period, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice…"

Previously the alias parenthetical sat between the party name and the verb, so no contiguous "Customer may terminate … for convenience" existed on the face of the clause. The substantive bargain is identical — same party, same unconditional election, same 30-day notice, same pro-rata refund.

Everything else is held as validated:

- **One insertion, nothing deleted.** 18.1, 18.2, the paragraph 3 Management Committee gate, paragraph 23 default remedies, and the capital-cost sentence all survive verbatim.
- **Element 4 remains already_met** on the retained 18.1 quote; no reciprocal or restated grant for the counterparties.
- **No extras:** no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, notice procedure, or damages categories.
- **Numbering retained in the operative text ("18.1A")**, so the forfeiture sentence — keyed expressly to "Subparagraph 18.1" — cannot attach to our withdrawal. Per the verifier's note, I left that sentence alone rather than expanding 18.1A; the money term belongs to the liquidated-damages rule.
- **Fallback deliberately not pursued** (30 days sits outside the 60–90 day band); the preferred checklist is complete, and the comment offers the 60–90 day / three-month-cap fallback as a negotiating trade.
